rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as a single mass, so it passes basic visual unity, but the form is too generic and too sealed for a gymnasium brief. The stepped roof is regular and not overly stair-like, yet it behaves as repetitive tiering rather than an expressive long-span section. Most critically, the verified frontage edge is met by a sealed perimeter with no legible public void, undercut, entry seam, or ground-level threshold response. That breaks the site-access semantic and leaves the dominant mass looking like a compact object rather than one usable hall with subordinate entry/service logic. The geometry is also not well aligned with the program’s required clear-span and roof/daylight section invariants: the silhouette suggests stacked horizontal bands instead of a hall section that reads as spanning space. Because of this, the form is not program-fit even though it is repaired cleanly and avoids obvious self-collision.
